walkthroughs.body_html:
Voice of the Genome — a core area of A-Level Biology.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Voice of the Genome brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Voice of the Genome.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: Gametes are produced by which type of cell division?
options: meiosis
mitosis
binary fission
budding

mcqs.q: A cell becomes specialised mainly by:
options: switching particular genes on or off
losing the genes it does not need
gaining extra chromosomes
changing its DNA bases

mcqs.q: A totipotent stem cell is one that can:
options: develop into any cell type, including extra-embryonic tissue
only become a red blood cell
no longer divide
make only nerve cells

mcqs.q: The acrosome reaction allows a sperm to:
options: digest through the egg's outer layers
swim faster towards the egg
copy the egg's DNA
divide into many sperm

mcqs.q: Why do specialised cells differ if they share the same DNA?
options: Specialised cells differ because they contain different genes.
All body cells carry the same genes, but different genes are switched on or off, so each cell makes different proteins.
Specialised cells lose the genes they don't need.
A totipotent cell cannot divide.

mcqs.q: How many chromosomes do gametes have compared with body cells?
options: A totipotent cell cannot divide.
Gametes have twice as many chromosomes as body cells.
Gametes have the same number of chromosomes as body cells.
Gametes are haploid, with half the chromosome number of diploid body cells, restored to diploid at fertilisation.

mcqs.q: What can a totipotent stem cell do?
options: Gametes have twice as many chromosomes as body cells.
A totipotent cell can only become one specific type of cell.
It can divide and differentiate into any cell type, including the extra-embryonic tissues such as the placenta.
A totipotent cell cannot divide.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Differentiation”?
options: A protein that binds to DNA and switches genes on or off, controlling which proteins a cell makes and therefore its phenotype.
An undifferentiated cell that can divide and differentiate into specialised cell types; it may be totipotent, pluripotent or multipotent.
The release of enzymes from the sperm's acrosome that digest the egg's outer layers, allowing one sperm to fertilise the egg.
The process by which an unspecialised cell becomes specialised by switching particular genes on or off to make specific proteins.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Transcription factor”?
options: A haploid sex cell, sperm or egg, produced by meiosis that fuses with another gamete at fertilisation to restore the diploid number.
The process by which an unspecialised cell becomes specialised by switching particular genes on or off to make specific proteins.
A reduction division producing four genetically varied haploid cells, generating variation through crossing over and independent assortment.
A protein that binds to DNA and switches genes on or off, controlling which proteins a cell makes and therefore its phenotype.

mcqs.q: Which of these is the best definition of “Gamete”?
options: A protein that binds to DNA and switches genes on or off, controlling which proteins a cell makes and therefore its phenotype.
A reduction division producing four genetically varied haploid cells, generating variation through crossing over and independent assortment.
The release of enzymes from the sperm's acrosome that digest the egg's outer layers, allowing one sperm to fertilise the egg.
A haploid sex cell, sperm or egg, produced by meiosis that fuses with another gamete at fertilisation to restore the diploid number.

A haploid sex cell, sperm or egg, produced by meiosis that fuses with another gamete at fertilisation to restore the diploid number.

options: An undifferentiated cell that can divide and differentiate into specialised cell types; it may be totipotent, pluripotent or multipotent.

free_texts.hint: It's one of the six key terms above.

sequence.def: Chromosomes condense; nuclear envelope breaks down
Chromosomes line up at the cell equator
Sister chromatids pulled to opposite poles
Nuclei reform around the two sets of chromosomes
Cytoplasm divides, forming two identical cells
